statement: Typed scientific knowledge about quantities: what a quantity is (kind, dimension), how it is expressed (units and their properties), which quantities are defined by a method (metrics) and which conditions make results comparable. General physics and metrology, never product facts. Written in PEE's own words; facts only, no third-party text reproduced. v2 (2026-10-18) adds test methods with their fixed conditions, physical and definitional relations, ordinal class scales, and label-reading language; entries prompted by the owner's category research packages are verified against the sources they name before inclusion. qk.2.5 (S103): the bound words of the retired Phase253 local request reader are pack data (one bound reader for requests and documents).
dimensionNote: SI base quantities (length, mass, time, electric current, thermodynamic temperature, amount of substance, luminous intensity). Plane and solid angle are dimensionless, so luminance (cd/m2) and illuminance (lx) share a dimension and are told apart by their units and kinds, never by dimension alone.

kinds.note: Celsius and Fahrenheit are offset scales: a temperature converts with an offset, a temperature difference without one.
Energy per counted operation (kWh per cycle, kWh/100 cycles): compared only on the same basis and programme.
Volume per counted operation (litres per cycle).

Energy stated per reference period (kWh/annum, kWh/year). Dimensionally a power, but a different quantity from rated or average power: a declared kWh/annum may rest on a conventional number of cycles, so it never converts to watts or to another period.
How many times per hour a volume of air equal to the room volume passes through the cleaner: a rate, not a flow.
Volume per reference period (litres per day of a dehumidifier, litres per year); like periodic energy, compared only on the same basis and conditions.
Depends on the distance and the room: without the measurement distance two sound pressure levels are not comparable.
kinds.plain: the noise level measured at some distance from the appliance (sound pressure level, which depends on the distance and the room)

kinds.note: A property of the source, independent of distance; what EU energy labels declare. Never comparable with a sound pressure level measured at a distance. It is determined from sound pressure measured over an enveloping surface or in a reverberation room (ISO 3741/3744) and is reported as a result by laboratories and on EU labels (dB(A) re 1 pW); that a source measured a value does not say whether it reports pressure or power.
kinds.plain: the noise emission the maker declares, as on EU energy labels (sound power level, independent of distance)

kinds.note: Water removed per unit of electrical energy (L/kWh): dehumidifier energy factor.
A colour difference (ΔE) is dimensionless and depends on the formula (CIE76, CIE94, CIEDE2000): values from different formulas are different quantities.
Relative humidity (%RH) is a ratio of dimension one; a percentage is relative humidity only when the words say so.

conditionAxes.note: the test method or rating scheme a value was produced under; filled from the methods section
dry-bulb temperature and relative humidity of the air a dehumidifier processes; capacity depends on both; the two are read together as one condition (a rating point)
input resolution, refresh rate and picture/game mode of a display latency or motion test
the electrical input at which a loudspeaker level is measured (1 W, or 2.83 V = 1 W into 8 Ω)

metrics.label: clean air delivery rate

definedBy.method: ENERGY STAR room air cleaner test (AHAM AC-1)

metrics.note: A whole-device rate of particle removal for one challenge; free fan airflow, filter class and room-size claims do not establish it.

metrics.label: fan airflow
metrics.note: The air the fan moves, not the clean air delivered: it can be far higher than CADR.

metrics.label: recommended room size
metrics.note: Derived from CADR under an assumed number of air changes per hour and ceiling height; different assumptions give different sizes.

metrics.label: declared A-weighted sound power level (EU energy label)
metrics.note: Declared by the supplier in the eco programme; a tester's sound-meter reading is a sound pressure level and does not confirm or contradict it directly. Audit S77 (A1-3, A1-5): the generic term "energy label" no longer settles this metric (a mention of an energy label is not a noise-emission value; average or full-screen brightness is not peak luminance; Bluetooth latency is not input lag).

metrics.label: peak luminance
metrics.note: Depends on the measured window size and duration. Audit S77 (A1-3, A1-5): the generic term "brightness" no longer settles this metric (a mention of an energy label is not a noise-emission value; average or full-screen brightness is not peak luminance; Bluetooth latency is not input lag).

metrics.label: moisture removal capacity
metrics.note: Water removed per day at stated air conditions; a warmer, wetter rating point gives a much larger figure, so capacities under different conditions are not comparable.

conventionalBasis.note: capacity is reported per 24 h under the test procedures

metrics.label: water tank capacity
metrics.note: How much water the container holds before emptying; not how much the machine removes.

metrics.label: filter efficiency class (EN 1822 / ISO 29463)
metrics.note: The filter medium or element efficiency at the most penetrating particle size; it says nothing about the whole device airflow, bypass or the clean air delivered. "HEPA" names the filter (a class on en_1822_filter_class), not a percentage: a percentage near the word is not this efficiency unless efficiency is named (KN correction 2026-10-18).

metrics.label: advertised suction (Pa)
metrics.note: A manufacturer figure; the standard robot performance tests measure debris removal, not suction pressure.

metrics.label: pump pressure rating
metrics.note: The pump rating, not the pressure at the coffee bed.

metrics.label: colour gamut coverage
metrics.note: A percentage of a named reference gamut; coverage of different references is a different quantity.

metrics.label: input lag
metrics.note: Audit S77 (A1-3, A1-5): the generic term "latency" no longer settles this metric (a mention of an energy label is not a noise-emission value; average or full-screen brightness is not peak luminance; Bluetooth latency is not input lag).

metrics.label: loudspeaker sensitivity
metrics.note: Sound pressure at 1 m for 1 W or for 2.83 V input; 2.83 V delivers 1 W only into 8 Ω (2 W into 4 Ω), so the two ratings differ for low-impedance speakers.

units.note: US liquid gallon; a UK gallon is 4.54609 L: a page that does not say which is ambiguous
US liquid pint (US dehumidifier capacities); a UK pint is 0.56826125 L
per year / per annum is a reporting basis that may be conventional (a stated number of cycles)
the symbol K alone is not read: "4K" is a display resolution
also the width axis letter in "20 W x 30 H": see language.axisLetters
nit is a name for cd/m2
a counted operation: per cycle or per 100 cycles is a reporting basis, compared only on the same basis

en.comparativeNote: 'X-er than N' bounds the quantity from below when X-er is an increase and from above when it is a decrease; 'no/not X-er than N' reverses it. This is English, not physics, and is stated per word.
en.axisNote: a single capital W, H, D or L between numbers joined by x or × names a dimension axis (width, height, depth, length), not a unit

evaluation.note: polarity words; a negator within three words before flips the polarity; both polarities in one statement give mixed

qualitative.note: reading vocabulary for the structured qualitative model; a statement can be an observation (what was perceived), a judgement (an evaluation), or both

en.boundWordNote: S103: 'min' after a number is not a bound word: it is also the symbol of the minute ('40 min.'), and readers that pass the number's span alone would read the unit as a minimum (found on spent S89-S99 pages: 7 run times). 'min' before a number ('min. 5 litres') stays a bound word.

scope.statement: R3-P (owner authorisation 2026-10-20): one English vocabulary for clause boundaries, negation scope, polarity and contrast, read by src/language_scope.ts for requests and documents alike. A negator governs the words after it in its own clause, over at most maxScopeWords words, and stops at a number, a clause boundary or a contrast marker. A negator followed by a requirement word before the governed words negates the requirement ('I don't need more than 6 L': 6 L is enough), not the proposition ('nothing over 6 L': at most 6 L). English, not physics; stated per word.
scope.adjunctNote: Documents only (maskNegated): a cue inside a prepositional adjunct names the source or setting of the statement, not the negated predicate ("we did not notice any noise from our unit" is still the publisher's observation of its unit); a preposition right after the negator is inside the scope ("not from the manufacturer"). Requests keep the plain scope ("I don't want a model with wifi" rejects wifi).

relations.statement: The floor area a clean air delivery rate serves at a given number of air changes per hour and ceiling height: area = CADR × 60 / (ACH × height).

relations.caveat: Exact for a constant power; a varying power needs the average over the time.
relations.statement: Energy is power multiplied by time.

relations.caveat: Holds only for the same programme and conditions.
relations.statement: A value per 100 cycles divided by 100 is the value per cycle under the same programme and conditions.

relations.caveat: Free field and point source; indoors reflections make the fall-off smaller.
relations.statement: In a free field a point source loses 20·log10(d2/d1) dB of sound pressure level between distances d1 and d2 (about 6 dB per doubling); rooms add reflected sound, so this holds only approximately indoors.

relations.caveat: Resistive load; a loudspeaker impedance is nominal and varies with frequency.
relations.statement: Electrical power into a resistive load is V²/R: 2.83 V gives 1 W into 8 Ω and 2 W into 4 Ω.

an annoyance from tonal noise is not captured by a level alone
